name: Mr Mole
waitingLines: Hm. Comfy chair. I’ll stay till {partner}’s back. Haven’t said hi yet.
Hm. Mabel says don’t leave before greeting everyone. So. Waiting for {partner}.

questions.scene: Mr Mole slides a blurry photo across the table. It's a nose. A very weird nose.
lines: Hm. My cousin. Don't stare. Okay, stare a little.
questions.question: The star-nosed mole holds a world record. For what?

choices.label: Fastest eater of any mammal
reply: Hm. Correct. Blink and lunch is over.
His 22 nose tentacles find and gulp food in about a quarter second.
Mabel calls him 'the vacuum.' Not to his face.

choices.label: Loudest sneeze
reply: Hm. With that nose? Fair guess.
It's actually the fastest-eating mammal. Snack gone in about a quarter second.
Those 22 nose tentacles move faster than you can blink.

choices.label: Longest nap
reply: Hm. That's my record, not his.
He's the fastest eater of any mammal. A bite takes about a quarter second.
Family dinners are short. Very short.

questions.factBasis: The star-nosed mole is the fastest-eating mammal (~1/4 second per item); its star has 22 appendages.

questions.scene: Mr Mole sniffs the air by your open window, very slowly, eyes closed.
lines: Hm. Rain's coming. I can smell it. So can you, probably.
questions.question: That lovely 'smell of rain' on dry ground mostly comes from what?

choices.label: Clouds rubbing together
reply: Hm. Clouds don't rub. They hover.
It's mostly geosmin, made by soil bacteria, launched up by raindrops.
We can smell tiny amounts of it. Built-in rain alarm.

choices.label: Worms celebrating
reply: Hm. They do celebrate. Not the smell, though.
It's geosmin from soil bacteria, tossed into the air by raindrops.
That earthy smell even has a name: petrichor.

choices.label: Soil bacteria releasing a compound called geosmin
reply: Hm. Correct. Bacteria. Romantic, isn't it.
Rain kicks geosmin into the air, and human noses are incredibly sensitive to it.
The smell even has a name: petrichor. Mabel's favorite word.

questions.factBasis: Petrichor's earthy note is largely geosmin from soil microbes; humans detect it at very low concentrations.

questions.scene: A worm pokes out of your plant pot. Mr Mole tips his hat to it.
lines: Hm. Respect the worm. It has more heart than you.
questions.question: How many heart-like pumps does an earthworm have?

choices.label: One, like everybody else
reply: Hm. Reasonable. Also wrong.
Earthworms have five heart-like arches pumping blood.
Five hearts and still no drama. Admirable.

choices.label: Five
reply: Hm. Correct. Five little pumps.
They're called aortic arches, wrapped around the front of the worm.
Five hearts. Still can't say 'I love you.' Relatable.

choices.label: Zero. Cold-hearted
reply: Hm. Harsh on my coworker.
They've got five heart-like pumps. More than any of us.
Lots of heart. Very little brain. Honestly, peaceful.

questions.factBasis: Earthworms have five pairs of aortic arches, often called 'hearts'.

questions.scene: Mr Mole taps the ground with his paw and listens, impressed.
lines: Hm. Biggest living thing I know of. It's underground. Of course.
questions.question: One of the largest living organisms on Earth is a...?

choices.label: Blue whale
reply: Hm. Big. Not biggest by area.
A honey fungus in Oregon spreads underground across about 2,000+ acres.
Mostly hidden threads in the soil. Very mole of it.

choices.label: Giant honey fungus underground in Oregon
reply: Hm. Correct. A mushroom the size of a town.
Its threads spread across roughly 2,000+ acres of forest soil.
Possibly thousands of years old. Quiet achiever. My hero.

choices.label: Giant sequoia tree
reply: Hm. Tall. Impressive. Not the winner by area.
A honey fungus in Oregon covers about 2,000+ acres underground.
You walk over it and never know. Like most good things.

questions.factBasis: An Armillaria ostoyae individual in Oregon's Malheur National Forest spans ~2,385 acres.

questions.scene: Mr Mole presses one ear to the ground, listening to something you can't hear.
lines: Hm. The trees are gossiping again.
questions.question: Underground, many trees are linked together by what?

choices.label: Fungus threads that share nutrients
reply: Hm. Correct. Fungus is the real networker.
Fungal threads wrap roots and help move water and nutrients between trees.
Nicknamed the wood wide web. No password needed.

choices.label: Secret tunnels dug by moles
reply: Hm. I wish I got the credit.
It's fungi. Their threads link roots and pass nutrients around.
People call it the 'wood wide web.' Trees with a group chat.

choices.label: Root Wi-Fi with actual bars
reply: Hm. Close, honestly. Still wrong.
It's fungus threads linking roots, nicknamed the wood wide web.
No signal bars. Just mushrooms doing logistics.

questions.factBasis: Mycorrhizal fungal networks connect tree roots and move nutrients ('wood wide web').

questions.scene: Mr Mole opens his lunchbox. Something inside wiggles. He closes it very calmly.
lines: Hm. Don't worry about it. Actually, quiz about it.
questions.question: Some moles keep a pantry of live earthworms. How do they stop them escaping?

choices.label: A tiny fridge
reply: Hm. No outlets down here. Sadly.
They bite the worm's head so it's paralyzed but still fresh.
Hundreds stored at once. A pantry with a pulse.

choices.label: Asking them nicely to stay
reply: Hm. Worms don't respect manners.
Moles bite the head to paralyze them, so they keep for later.
The original meal prep. No containers, no dishes.

choices.label: A bite that paralyzes them
reply: Hm. Correct. Grim, but efficient.
A bite to the head means the worm stays alive but can't crawl off.
Some larders hold hundreds. Meal prep king.

questions.factBasis: Moles bite earthworms' heads to immobilize them and store them alive in larders.

questions.scene: Mr Mole sets down a photo of a little seabird with an orange beak.
lines: Hm. Fellow tunnel person. Different neighborhood.
questions.question: What's special about where Atlantic puffins nest?

choices.label: They nest on floating ice
reply: Hm. Cold. No.
They dig burrows in cliffs and often reuse them with the same partner.
Seabirds with tunnels. Respect.

choices.label: They borrow other birds' nests every year
reply: Hm. Rude. No.
Puffins dig their own burrows, often returning to the same one with the same mate.
Commitment, with a front door.

choices.label: They dig burrows and often return to the same one with the same mate
reply: Hm. Correct. Same burrow. Same partner. Year after year.
Puffins dig underground nests on cliff tops.
Mabel and I approve. Strongly.

questions.factBasis: Atlantic puffins nest in burrows and often reuse them with the same mate across years.

questions.scene: Mr Mole sits beside you on the couch. Not too close. Then a little closer.
lines: Hm. Mabel and I sit like this. Science says something about it.
questions.question: When romantic partners sit close together, what can happen to their bodies?

choices.label: They both get hungry at the same moment
reply: Hm. That's just dinnertime.
Studies found partners' breathing and heart rhythms can sync up.
Bodies in step. No talking required. My favorite kind of communication.

choices.label: Their breathing and heart rhythms can start to sync
reply: Hm. Correct. Studies found couples' heart rhythms and breathing can sync up.
Being near your person literally tunes your body to them.
Twenty years. Mabel and I probably hum in harmony now.

choices.label: Nothing. Bodies don't care
reply: Hm. Bodies care more than mouths do.
Partners' heart rhythms and breathing can sync when they're together.
Love is a quiet duet. Hm.

questions.factBasis: Studies (e.g., UC Davis 2012) observed physiological synchrony (breathing, heart rate) between romantic partners.

questions.scene: Mr Mole pulls a purple carrot out of the soil and holds it up.
lines: Hm. Not dyed. Not broken. Original.
questions.question: What color were most cultivated carrots before orange became popular?

choices.label: Purple or yellow
reply: Hm. Correct. Purple and yellow carrots came first.
Orange carrots became widespread later, especially through Dutch growers.
Mabel says purple ones taste fancier. She's right. Don't tell her.

choices.label: Bright blue
reply: Hm. Blue food makes me nervous.
Early carrots were mostly purple or yellow.
Orange took over later. Carrots had a rebrand.

choices.label: Always orange
reply: Hm. History disagrees.
Early cultivated carrots were mostly purple or yellow.
Orange became popular later. Even vegetables have eras.

questions.factBasis: Early domesticated carrots were mainly purple and yellow; orange cultivars were popularized in the 17th-century Netherlands.

questions.scene: Mr Mole points at a beach photo, then at a tiny drawing of a turtle hatchling.
lines: Hm. Long trip home. Very long.
questions.question: Where do many female sea turtles return to lay their eggs?

choices.label: Whichever beach has the best snacks
reply: Hm. Practical. Not it.
Many return to the beach region where they hatched, decades later.
Magnetic navigation. No maps. Very impressive.

choices.label: The same beach region where they hatched
reply: Hm. Correct. Decades later. Same beach.
They likely navigate using Earth's magnetic field.
Coming home after a long time away. Mabel cried at this one.

choices.label: A different ocean every time
reply: Hm. Too much travel.
Many return to the region where they hatched.
Sometimes decades later. That's commitment to a place.

questions.factBasis: Many sea turtles show natal homing, likely using geomagnetic cues.

questions.scene: Mr Mole fiddles with a small trowel, avoiding eye contact.
lines: Hm. Personal question. Don't make it weird.
questions.question: Saying 'I love you': out loud, or through actions?

choices.label: Out loud
reply: Hm. Out loud. Brave.
I said it once in 2006. Mabel wrote down the date.

choices.label: Through actions
reply: Hm. Actions. My people.
Twenty years. Twenty windows. Zero speeches.

A:A: You both say it out loud. Hm. Loud house.
{partner} says it, you say it back. Very efficient.
Mabel would cry. Happy crying.
A:B: Actions for you. {partner} likes hearing it out loud.
Hm. Mabel's the same. I learned to say it on Sundays.
Fix the shelf, then say the words. Double points.
B:A: You say it out loud. {partner} shows it instead.
So when they refill your water without asking? That's a whole love letter.
Read the actions. Say the words. Balanced.
B:B: Both of you, actions over words. Hm. Respect.
Your home must be full of fixed hinges and warm tea.
Still. Say it to {partner} once a year. For safety.

questions.scene: Mr Mole taps a wobbly shelf on your wall. It wobbles more.
lines: Hm. Who built this. Never mind.
questions.question: Home repair day: DIY it together, or hire a pro?

choices.label: DIY it together
reply: Hm. DIY. You, a toolbox, and hope.
I dug every window myself. Mabel only cried twice.

choices.label: Hire a pro
reply: Hm. Hire a pro. Wise.
Fewer fights about which way the screw turns.

A:A: Both pick DIY. Hm. Bold.
Buy extra screws. And extra patience for {partner}.
Crooked shelves hold the best memories.
A:B: You'd hire a pro. {partner} wants to grab the drill.
Hm. Let them try. Keep the pro's number on the fridge.
Mabel calls this 'supervising.' I call it love.
B:A: You want to DIY. {partner} wants to call someone.
Hm. Classic standoff. Try one small shelf first.
If it wobbles, call the pro. No shame.
B:B: You both hire a pro. Hm. Peaceful household.
No 'you're holding it wrong' fights with {partner}. Ever.
Spend the saved energy on snacks.

questions.scene: Mr Mole squints at your window and measures it with his paw.
lines: Hm. I dig windows. Professionally. Romantically.
questions.question: Dream window view: a garden, the night sky, or a rainy street?

choices.label: A garden
reply: Hm. A garden. Classic.
Mabel's first window faced her tomatoes. She talks to them daily.

choices.label: The night sky
reply: Hm. Night sky. Romantic.
Hard to dig toward. Worth it.

choices.label: A rainy street
reply: Hm. Rainy street. Moody.
Good for sitting. Good for not talking.

A:A: A garden for both of you. Hm. Easy.
Grow tomatoes with {partner}. Name them. Mabel did.
Don't get attached. They become sauce.
A:B: Night sky for you. {partner} picked the garden.
Hm. Plant flowers that bloom at night. Moonflowers exist.
Garden for them. Stars for you. One window.
A:C: Rainy street for you. {partner} wants a garden.
Hm. Rainy garden. Both happy. Worms happiest.
B:A: You want a garden. {partner} wants the night sky.
Hm. Easy fix. Garden window by day, roof window by night.
I dug Mabel both. It took two anniversaries.
B:B: Both pick the night sky. Hm. Stargazers.
Put the bed under it. Fall asleep counting stars with {partner}.
Mabel counts stars. I count Mabel. Hm. Too much?
B:C: Hm. Get one big window. Let the sky pick the mood.
Rain one night, stars the next. Nobody loses.
C:A: Garden for you, rainy street for {partner}.
Hm. Rain waters the garden. Same team, technically.
Watch it rain on the flowers together.
C:B: Hm. Unlucky. Clouds block stars. Weather picks favorites.
Rainy nights for {partner}, clear nights for you. Shared custody.
C:C: Rainy street for both. Hm. Cozy weirdos.
Tea, blanket, rain sounds, {partner}. No talking needed.
Best date. Zero effort. My kind.

questions.scene: Mr Mole sets two bowls of stew on your table and sits. Silently.
lines: Hm. ...Hm.
questions.question: Dinner for two: comfy silence, or nonstop chatting?

choices.label: Comfy silence
reply: Hm. Silence. My love language.
Mabel and I once didn't talk for an entire stew. Best dinner.

choices.label: Nonstop chatting
reply: Hm. Chatting. Lively.
Mabel tells stories. I nod. It's a system.

A:A: Both pick comfy silence. Hm. Rare skill.
Some couples need to talk. You and {partner} just pass the salt.
That's peak comfort. Trust me.
A:B: You want to chat. {partner} wants quiet.
Hm. Talk through the main course. Silence for dessert.
Pudding should be eaten in peace anyway.
B:A: You like quiet. {partner} likes to chat.
Hm. Be the nodder. It's a respected position.
Toss in 'really?' every few minutes. Works for me.
B:B: Both pick nonstop chatting. Hm. Loud table.
Hm. you and {partner} never finish soup while it's hot, do you.
Microwave it. Keep talking.

questions.scene: Mr Mole pulls out a tiny calendar with one date circled. Hard.
lines: Hm. Anniversary talk. My specialty. Quietly.
questions.question: Anniversaries: a big celebration, or the same quiet tradition every year?

choices.label: A big celebration
reply: Hm. Big. Balloons. Noise.
I'd hide under the table. But good for you.

choices.label: A quiet tradition
reply: Hm. Same tradition every year. Correct answer.
Twenty years. Twenty windows. Never once boring.

A:A: Both want big celebrations. Hm. Party couple.
Invite everyone. Make {partner} give a speech.
I would leave early. You won't.
A:B: You love a quiet tradition. {partner} wants it big.
Hm. Let them throw the party. You sneak in the ritual.
A toast for two, mid-party. Mabel likes that.
B:A: You want a big party. {partner} wants the quiet tradition.
Hm. Do the tradition at sunrise. Party at night.
Two celebrations. Twice the cake.
B:B: You both want a quiet tradition. Hm. Perfect.
Same spot, same meal with {partner}, every year. That's a love story.
Mabel calls ours 'window day.' Find yours.

questions.scene: Mr Mole kneels by your sink, listening to a drip with deep concern.
lines: Hm. That drip. It's mocking us.
questions.question: When something breaks at home, what does your partner do?
questions.selfQuestion: When something breaks at home, what do you do?

choices.label: Fixes it (eventually)
reply: Hm. 'Eventually.' Love that word.
My gutter's been 'almost fixed' since spring.

choices.label: Calls for help right away
reply: Hm. Calls for help. Efficient.
Nothing wrong with knowing your limits.

A:A: You fix it yourself, and {partner} knew it. Hm.
They've watched you mutter at a broken drawer before.
'Eventually' is a valid timeline.
A:B: You'd call for help. {partner} pictured you with a wrench.
Hm. They believe in you more than your skills do.
Call the pro. Keep the wrench as decoration.
B:A: You'd fix it yourself. {partner} thought you'd call someone.
Hm. Underestimated. Go get the toolbox.
Let them watch. Quietly impressed is a love language.
B:B: Help on speed dial, and {partner} called it. Hm.
No pretending to understand pipes. Healthy.
Mole wisdom: wet floors don't care about pride.

questions.scene: Mr Mole quietly slides the last cookie toward you, then looks away.
lines: Hm. That wasn't anything. Moving on.
questions.question: Which tiny thing does your partner do that secretly means 'I love you'?
questions.selfQuestion: Which tiny thing do you do that secretly means 'I love you'?

choices.label: Saves the last bite
reply: Hm. The last bite. Real sacrifice.
Mabel gives me hers. I pretend I didn't notice. I noticed.

choices.label: Warms up the bed first
reply: Hm. Bed warming. Underrated.
Cold sheets are a crime. They're a hero.

choices.label: Texts 'home safe?'
reply: Hm. 'Home safe?' Short. Strong.
Two words that carry all the other words.

A:A: The last bite, and {partner} saw it coming. Hm.
They noticed every fry you've ever given up.
That's real love. Food love.
A:B: You warm the bed. {partner} guessed the last bite.
Hm. They think the mattress is just naturally cozy.
Leave a note on the pillow. 'This was me.'
A:C: You send 'home safe?' {partner} guessed the last bite.
Hm. They think your love language is fries. It's also texts.
Do both. Text from the table. Pass the fries.
B:A: You give up the last bite. {partner} guessed bed warming.
Hm. They missed all the fries you sacrificed.
Next time, slide it over slowly. Make eye contact.
B:B: Warming the bed, and {partner} knew. Hm.
They clocked the warm sheets. Every single time.
Human heater. Respected profession.
B:C: 'Home safe?' is your love note. {partner} guessed bed warming.
Hm. They're giving the blanket your credit.
Fine. Warm the bed too. Overachiever.
C:A: Last bite for you. {partner} guessed the 'home safe?' text.
Hm. They're reading your texts, not your plate.
Text 'saved you the last bite.' Both covered.
C:B: Bed warming is your move. {partner} guessed the texts.
Hm. Your best work, completely uncredited. Classic.
Text them: 'Bed's warm.' Now they'll know.
C:C: Short texts. Huge meaning. They get it.
Mabel texts me that. From the next room.

questions.scene: A spider strolls across your ceiling. Mr Mole watches it, unbothered.
lines: Hm. Roommate. Doesn't pay rent.
questions.question: There's a spider in the house. What does your partner do?
questions.selfQuestion: There's a spider in the house. What do you do?

choices.label: Gently carries it outside
reply: Hm. Spider escort. Gentle soul.
Mabel does this. She names them first.

choices.label: Calls for backup
reply: Hm. Backup. Smart. Spiders are fast.
No shame. I scream too. Quietly.

A:A: Spider escort, and {partner} knew. Hm.
Cup, paper, calm face, out the door.
That spider tells all its friends about you.
A:B: You'd call for backup. {partner} thought you were the brave one.
Hm. Your secret's out.
Good news: now they know to come running.
B:A: You'd walk the spider out. {partner} thought you'd yell for help.
Hm. They don't know you're the spider whisperer.
Show them next time. Very casually.
B:B: Calling for backup, and {partner} knew it. Hm.
They already know their role: spider bodyguard.
Teamwork. One screams, one carries.

questions.scene: Mr Mole lies flat on your rug and stares at the ceiling. Peacefully.
lines: Hm. Sunday energy. Let's discuss.
questions.question: Lazy Sunday. What does your partner actually want to do?
questions.selfQuestion: Lazy Sunday. What do you actually want to do?

choices.label: Fix a few things around the house
reply: Hm. Productive Sunday. Suspicious.
Mabel calls it 'puttering.' I respect it.

choices.label: Absolutely nothing
reply: Hm. Nothing. A noble goal.
Sundays were made for staring at ceilings.

A:A: Fixing stuff, and {partner} knew. Hm.
They've seen you 'relax' while holding a screwdriver.
Let them nap nearby. You putter.
A:B: You want to do nothing. {partner} thought you'd be fixing things.
Hm. Busted. The tools stay in the drawer.
Tell them gently: Sunday is a no-hammer zone.
B:A: You'd want to fix stuff. {partner} thought you'd do nothing.
Hm. Surprise handyman. Plot twist.
Fix one thing, then do nothing together. Fair trade.
B:B: Absolutely nothing, and {partner} knew. Hm.
Pajamas. No plans. No guilt.
Perfect Sunday. Mole approved.

questions.scene: Mr Mole shows you a small window he dug for Mabel. He looks very proud. Says nothing.
lines: Hm. About being proud. Quietly.
questions.question: When your partner is secretly proud of you, what do they do?
questions.selfQuestion: When you're secretly proud of your partner, what do you do?

choices.label: Tells everyone
reply: Hm. A hype person. Loud love.
Mabel tells the whole tunnel when I fix a window.

choices.label: Says 'hm, nice' and smiles
reply: Hm. 'Hm, nice.' My entire vocabulary.
Means more than it sounds. Trust me.

A:A: You tell everyone, and {partner} knew. Hm.
Your group chat has heard about them. Many times.
Keep going. They act embarrassed. They're not.
A:B: Just 'hm, nice' from you. {partner} imagined a whole parade.
Hm. Lower their expectations or raise your volume.
Tell one person. Out loud. Where they can hear.
B:A: You tell everyone. {partner} thought you'd just say 'hm, nice.'
Hm. They have no idea about your bragging.
Forward them one hype text. Let them see.
B:B: 'Hm, nice' and a smile, and {partner} knew. Hm.
They read that tiny smile like a full speech.
Mole-level communication. I'm proud. Hm. Nice.
